I've had really good success with this method over the course of this season so far, and of course I've been tweaking it since initially setting it up. This is very much based on fawkesmulder's post (within this subverse). Below are the advanced metrics I use for each position, or rather what I use to rate at each position:

  • Pitchers (16 total categories): Age, ERA, WHIP, xFIP, SIERA, SwStr%, F-Strike%, BABIP, K/9, K%, K-BB%, HR/9, GB%, IFFB%, Soft%, Hard%
  • Batters (19 total categories): Age, AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, BB%, K%, SwStr%, wOBA, wRC+, ISO, BABIP, HR/FB, O-Swing%, Z-Contact%, FB%, LD%, Soft%, Hard%

The method is to use the baseline for averages at each position (starting pitchers and batters) for that year. Then for each of these categories, give a point if the players metric is better than the average. Then take the total number of accumulated points, and divide it by the total number of categories to find the average. If you wanted to go a step farther, you could give weights to each categories as well (something I'm still looking into). I also keep track of trending for the batters.
